capitals.name: Sumur (Simyra)
capitals.note: Infobox capital Sumur; the Aziru page has Aziru 'captured the city of Sumur (Simyrra)' (undated) and the Kadesh page has Ramesses II securing 'the port of Sumur'. The page gives no coordinates; the dot is placed at Tartus, the nearest modern city, until a gap-filler locates Sumur.

correction.text: the territory 'between the Middle Orontes and the central Levantine coast' from Tartus in the north to Byblos in the south, across the Akkar plains and east to the Homs Gap

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no Amurru; its Hittite shape of -1300 (321,568 km2) swallows the coast. The page gives no area; it describes the land as the coast from Tartus to Byblos, the Akkar plains and the Orontes valley east to the Homs Gap. The shape is the researcher's union of the Tartus governorate (about 2,000 km2), North Lebanon (about 1,800 km2), a 25 km radius round Byblos and a 40 km radius round Homs, about 5,000 km2 in all. The Ugarit and Siyannu border is not drawn.

ledger.note: c. 1350 BC: Aziru's Amurru. The Aziru page gives 'Reign: c. 35 regnal years c. 1350~1315 BC' and has him 'captured the city of Sumur'; Abdi-Ashirta, 'the first documented leader of Amurru', is only 'fl. 14th century BC' on his page, so the start is a bridging judgment at Aziru's accession. The infobox 'Established: c. 2000 BCE' refers to the Amorite name, not to a kingdom.

ledger.note: c. 1350 BC: Amurru under Egyptian overlordship. The Amurru page has Aziru 'claimed to govern Amurru on Egypt's behalf' in the Amarna letters, while Akhenaten 'repeatedly asked Aziru to come to Egypt' (the Aziru page: the summons in EA 162, 'detained in Egypt for at least a year'); none of this is dated.

ledger.note: c. 1345 BC: Aziru leaves Egypt. 'He changed his allegiance to Suppiluliuma I around 1350-1345 BCE.'

ledger.note: c. 1345 BC: Amurru becomes a Hittite vassal. 'He changed his allegiance to Suppiluliuma I around 1350-1345 BCE'; the treaty is listed as 'Treaty of Suppiluliuma I with Aziru of Amurru (CTH 49)' with no year, and 'Amurru remained firmly in Hittite hands until the reign of the 19th Dynasty Pharaohs'. Mirrors the hittites dossier.

region.text: the territory 'between the Middle Orontes and the central Levantine coast' from Tartus in the north to Byblos in the south, across the Akkar plains and east to the Homs Gap

ledger.note: 1275 BC: Ramesses II invades Amurru. 'In the fourth year of his reign, he marched north into Syria to recapture Amurru'; 'In the previous year, Ramesses II had invaded the neighboring province of Amurru' before the battle of 'Year 5 III Shemu day 9' (May 1274 BC), so the invasion falls in 1275 BC. The page gives no BC year for the invasion itself.

ledger.note: 1275 BC: Amurru passes to Egypt. Ramesses II 'marched north into Syria to recapture Amurru' and left a Ne'arin troop there 'to secure the port of Sumur'.

region.text: the territory 'between the Middle Orontes and the central Levantine coast' from Tartus in the north to Byblos in the south, across the Akkar plains and east to the Homs Gap

ledger.note: 1274 BC: Egyptian influence over Amurru is lost after Kadesh. 'Egyptian influence over Amurru and Qadesh seems to have been lost forever'; 'Ramesses got the upper-hand at the end of Kadesh, but failed to retake Amurru and Qadesh'. The battle is dated May 1274 BC.

region.text: the territory 'between the Middle Orontes and the central Levantine coast' from Tartus in the north to Byblos in the south, across the Akkar plains and east to the Homs Gap

ledger.note: 1274 BC (bridged): Amurru is again a Hittite vassal. 'What exactly happened to Amurru is disputed'; 'At some point, both regions may have lapsed back under Hittite control'; Bryce thinks 'it is more likely Amurru remained a Hittite vassal state'; 'The recovery of Amurru was Muwatalli II's stated motivation for marching south'. The Amurru page, by contrast, has Amurru on the Egyptian side at Kadesh.

ledger.note: c. 1200 BC: the Hittite vassalage ends. The page says references to Amurru 'disappear with the Hittite Empire and Ugarit'; the hittites dossier ends the vassalage in 1180, the page puts the kingdom's end 'circa 1200 BC'.

ledger.note: c. 1200 BC: Amurru ends in the Bronze Age collapse. Infobox 'Disestablished: c. 1200 BCE'; the kingdom ended 'during the Bronze Age Collapse circa 1200 BC'. The page names no successor (it mentions Middle Assyrian and Phrygian activity afterwards).

wars.name: Aziru's wars against Byblos
wars.outcome: Rib-Hadda of Byblos 'was ultimately exiled'; Aziru captured Sumur; Egypt summoned Aziru (EA 162) and detained him for 'at least a year'. No border is dated.
wars.note: Undated on the page; the span is Aziru's accession to his change of allegiance (c. 1350-1345 BCE). Abdi-Ashirta's earlier conflict with Rib-Hadda is undated too ('fl. 14th century BC', Abdi-Ashirta page).

wars.outcome: Ramesses II invades Amurru in year 4 (1275 BC) and fights Muwatalli II at Kadesh in May 1274 BC; he 'failed to retake Amurru and Qadesh'; Amurru stays in the Hittite sphere (disputed).
wars.note: 'The recovery of Amurru was Muwatalli II's stated motivation for marching south to confront the Egyptians.' The page gives no treaty year for Amurru.

certainty.note: The page describes the land by features (coast, Akkar plains, Homs Gap), not a boundary.

sources.title: Battle of Kadesh
sources.note: May 1274 BC; Ramesses II's invasion of Amurru in the previous year; Amurru's fate after Kadesh disputed. The pages for Benteshina and Bentesina failed to load.

notes: Cliopatria has no Amurru. Dates are thin: Abdi-Ashirta's reign and Aziru's accession are 'fl. 14th century BC' and 'c. 1350~1315', so the 1350 start, the 1350/1345 allegiance changes and the 1200 end are bridges at confidence 1-2. The Benteshina page (the king reinstated under Urhi-Teshub, the treaty with Hatti, Amurru's Kadesh role) failed to load under https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benteshina and https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bentesina; a gap-filler should find its title. The Hittite dossier (me-04-a) mirrors the Egyptian dossier for -1275/-1274 and ends the vassalage in -1180, this dossier in -1200 (the page's date). The Amurru page has Amurru on the Egyptian side at Kadesh; the Kadesh page leans to a Hittite vassal (Bryce). Not drawn: Siyannu, Arwad, Byblos' dependent towns (page silent on the Eleutheros and Siyannu), the Ugarit boundary. The Sumur dot is a placeholder at Tartus.
